# ADR-068 — Checkpoint 10.1: Canvas LMS integration — read-only, PAT-authenticated, storage narrower than Canvas's shapes (migration 0020)

**Status:** Locked

<!-- Decision text below is verbatim from the pre-split docs/DECISIONS.md table row (2026-09-16). Do not edit a Locked decision without explicit owner approval. -->

**Checkpoint 10.1 — Canvas LMS integration: read-only, Personal-Access-Token authenticated, storage deliberately narrower than Canvas's own response shapes (2026-09-15, owner-approved).** One migration, `0020_canvas_lms_integration` (six new tables — `canvas_connections`, `canvas_courses`, `canvas_assignments`, `canvas_announcements`, `canvas_events`, `canvas_sync_runs` — level **21**). Phase 10 opened for consolidation and agent-readiness (Checkpoint 10.0); this is Phase 10's first product checkpoint and the first genuinely new external integration since Phase 7 (Gmail). **1. DISCOVERY WAS RE-VERIFIED LIVE, NOT ASSUMED.** A prior Canvas feasibility pass existed but left no recoverable artifact in this repository (confirmed by an exhaustive search: every branch, the full reflog, stash, a content pickaxe across all history, and every dangling/unreachable git object — none referenced Canvas). Rather than design against memory or documentation alone, a bounded, read-only, three-round probe was re-run live against the owner's real UTA Canvas account (`uta.instructure.com`) using a fresh Personal Access Token: `GET /users/self` (200, confirms auth + base URL), `/courses` with `include[]=term` (16 active courses, full field shape incl. term dates), `/courses/:id/assignments` with `include[]=submission` (the real per-user submission sub-object: `workflow_state`/`missing`/`late`/`submitted_at`/`score`/`grade`/`entered_score`/`entered_grade`/`attachments`, all populated and confirmed, not guessed), `/announcements` (a real non-empty example: HTML `message` field, 712 chars, no upstream bound), `/calendar_events?type=event` (endpoint reachable, zero live examples across every active course and an unscoped year-wide date range — recorded `observed: false` per the ADR-050/062 convention, not assumed from documentation), and `/planner/items` + `/users/self/upcoming_events` (evaluated as candidate sync sources, not adopted — see §4). Rate limit (`X-Rate-Limit-Remaining`) stayed at 700 across all ~15 requests. **No credential was persisted**: each round wrote the token to a file outside the git repository (the session scratchpad) and deleted it immediately after that round's probe, verified by directory listing; the token passed through conversation content, so the owner was advised to rotate it. **2. AUTH IS A PERSONAL ACCESS TOKEN, NOT OAUTH2, OWNER-CHOSEN.** A Canvas PAT already carries the full grant of the account — there is no finer OAuth scope to request that would narrow it further — and a Developer Key requires either self-service developer keys enabled on the institution's instance or an IT registration this single-user self-hosted app has no path to obtain. No redirect URI, no consent screen, no second credential lane: the owner pastes a PAT once, it is encrypted at rest with the existing `packages/ai-providers` AES-256-GCM ciphertext/iv/auth-tag triple (the `mail_connections` pattern, verbatim), and used for `GET` requests only. Canvas PATs are long-lived by default, so `canvas_connections` stores one credential triple, never a token-plus-refresh pair — there is no refresh flow to build. **3. STORAGE IS DELIBERATELY NARROWER THAN WHAT CANVAS RETURNS**, per an explicit "does this field need to exist locally for Personal OS functionality?" pass over every discovered field, run BEFORE schema design, not after: course rows keep name/code/term/enrollment-and-workflow-state/`html_url` and drop `uuid`, `license`, `calendar.ics`, `storage_quota_mb`, blueprint/template flags, `is_public*`, and every account/root-account id — none of it is Personal-OS-functional. Assignment rows keep title/`due_at`/`points_possible`/`submission_types`/`published`/`html_url` and three coarse submission fields the brief explicitly asked for (`submission_state`, `submission_missing`, `submission_late`, `submitted_at`). **Grade and score are excluded on purpose, not merely unrequested**: the live probe confirmed `score`/`grade`/`entered_score`/`entered_grade` are real, populated fields, and this checkpoint does not sync them — a grade is more FERPA-sensitive than "did I turn it in," the brief never asked for a gradebook, and adding grade columns later is a strictly additive migration, never a redesign. Submission `attachments` (the student's own uploaded work) are excluded at a higher sensitivity than description text for the same reason. **Assignment `description` and announcement `message` are never stored as the raw HTML Canvas returns.** Both are instructor-authored rich HTML of unbounded upstream size; this project has no HTML sanitizer or renderer, and React Native's `<Text>` interprets no markup (the same reasoning ADR-059 §5 already applies to search results). Assignment `description` is not stored at all — the functional ask is "what's due and when," and `html_url` is a one-tap deep link to Canvas for the full prompt. Announcement `message` **is** stored, because unlike an assignment prompt an announcement's entire value is its content — but only as a tag-stripped, truncated plain-text preview, bounded at write exactly like every provider-authored string in this codebase (`text-bounds.ts`'s convention: truncate, never reject, for text the owner didn't type). No genuine Canvas calendar event exists in the owner's account today; the sync stores real `calendar_events(type=event)` rows when they exist but ships with zero verified live examples — recorded honestly, not fabricated. Assignment due dates are **not** duplicated into `canvas_events`: the assignment row is the one source of a due instant, mirroring this project's standing rule against a second source of truth for calendar data. **4. SYNC IS PER-COURSE POLLING, NOT THE AGGREGATE PLANNER FEED.** `/planner/items` and `/users/self/upcoming_events` were both evaluated live and rejected as the primary source: `planner/items`'s `plannable` sub-object is a materially thinner projection than the full assignment/announcement resources (no `points_possible`, no `submission_types`, no full submission state), and `upcoming_events` only recasts near-term assignments as pseudo-events rather than surfacing genuine calendar events or full announcements. At 16 active courses and Canvas's evidently generous per-instance rate limit (unchanged across every probe), a full per-course sweep (courses → assignments+submission → announcements → calendar events, three to four calls per course) is well within budget for a cron-driven sync, mirroring this project's own per-course/per-metric polling precedent (Health's per-stream chunks, Gmail's per-mailbox history walk) rather than adopting an aggregate endpoint that would still need a full per-item re-fetch to get the fields this checkpoint requires. **5. IDEMPOTENCY, FAILURE CONTAINMENT AND RETENTION FOLLOW THE MAIL/HEALTH TEMPLATE EXACTLY, NOT A NEW DESIGN.** `onConflictDoUpdate` keyed on `(connection_id, canvas_*_id)` with a `setWhere` content-comparison gate so an unchanged row writes nothing (the `mail_messages` idiom, verbatim); a `canvas_sync_runs` row opened `failed` before any request goes out and flipped to its true terminal status on completion, so a killed process leaves evidence rather than silence; `failure_class`/`error_message` restricted to the same token-shaped regex `mail_sync_runs` enforces, so provider prose can never reach a log line or a database column; one course's failure is contained and the sweep continues to the next course (the `expand-window`/mail per-item containment precedent) rather than aborting the whole connection's sync; `canvas_sync_runs` joins the existing daily `retention.cleanup` job on the same 30-day `finished_at` window as `mail_sync_runs`/`health_sync_runs` — no new cron, no new schedule. **6. NO AI, NO MUTATIONS, NO NEW EGRESS SURFACE.** Per the brief's own explicit instruction, no Canvas content is summarized or sent to any model in this checkpoint; the integration writes only to its own six tables, touches no `ai_task_routes` row, and imports nothing from `ai` — confirmed to sit entirely outside both of `ai-egress-guard.test.ts`'s pinned surfaces (Guard 1's five call sites, Guard 4's `intelligence/` denylist) by construction, not by exemption. The integration is strictly read-only: no assignment submission, no announcement reply, no course-setting change — `packages/canvas-providers`'s client implements only `GET` methods, so a write is structurally absent from the interface, not merely policy-disallowed. **7. DEPLOYMENT IS DEFERRED TO THE OWNER'S OWN PRODUCTION ACCESS.** This checkpoint implements and locally verifies (migration reconciled, full monorepo test suite, typecheck, a security/privacy adversarial review) but does **not** run the frozen production deployment order in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — that requires the owner's own SSH access to the `personal-os` host, an EAS cloud build and a physical Rabbit R1 install, none of which this session can perform; owner-confirmed scope (2026-09-15). **Unchanged and reaffirmed:** ADR-018 (Tailscale-only; no Canvas webhook, no public ingress of any kind), ADR-024 (no backup system — Canvas data is a locally cached reflection of the institution's own record, not data Personal OS is the source of truth for, so its loss is recoverable by re-sync rather than irrecoverable), ADR-050 (CHECK only on project-controlled closed vocabularies — `canvas_connections.status` and `canvas_sync_runs.kind`/`status` are CHECKed; Canvas-defined vocabularies — `enrollment_state`, course `workflow_state`, `submission_state`, announcement `read_state` — are Zod-enforced only, since Canvas controls and can grow them), ADR-056 (no embeddings, no pgvector, no write-capable AI lane touched) (Checkpoint 10.1, 2026-09-15)
